messages:
sasha: FYI — customers are seeing dropped audit events during peak windows. stack shows validation failures and KMS timeouts. need quick sync on schema strictness vs cost/backpressure.
amar: any error samples? 400s or upstream timeouts?
jordyn: see spikes around 11:42-11:50 UTC — p95 ingest latency jumped to 2.3s, SQS queue depth spiked, few 5xx from our ingest workers. most common error is "validation_failed: missing field" and some KMS envelope decrypt timeouts.
lucy: are these customers on strict schema enforcement? some enterprise tenants requested strict validation for compliance.
sasha: mixed: some tenants opted-in strict, others on default lenient. problem is new schema change (payload.metadata.* is now required) — clients sending old shape. strict validation + high QPS => CPU and KMS ops skyrocketing.
amar: KMS is a big factor. decrypt per-event for signed payloads costs CPU and adds latency. we could validate signatures without full decrypt at the proxy to reduce work. suggestion: verify envelope signature and only decrypt in downstream where needed.
jordyn: other lever — move from per-event indexing to micro-batching + async indexing. that drops indexing IO and cost, but increases tail latency for availability queries. tradeoff: cost vs up-to-the-second visibility.
lucy: from compliance perspective some customers require every event fully validated and stored. we need per-tenant policy: strict (reject), buffered (accept but flag), lenient (accept best-effort). communicate clearly in API contract.
sasha: agreed. proposal: add tenant_ingest_policy with values [strict, buffered, lenient]. default buffered. buffered = accept events but mark "needs_validation" and surface to customer/ops.
amar: implementation notes: at the edge (ingest proxy) run lightweight schema check + signature verify. if failure and tenant=buffered => store raw to hot-s3 with minimal metadata and emit reject metric. if strict => reject 400. Also add token-level RBAC so only services with ingest:validate can call decrypt endpoints.
jordyn: backlog/backpressure options: a) 503 w/ Retry-After when queue > threshold, b) shed non-critical events (e.g., telemetry) with 429, c) offer per-tenant burst buckets. current preference: 503 for global backpressure and tenant-level burst tokens.
ingest-bot: ingest-proxy: throttled 42 requests at 2026-06-12T11:47:30Z, average retry-after 12s.
amar: quick config sketch: ```json
{
  "ingest": {
    "batch_window_ms": 150,
    "max_batch_size": 2048,
    "validation_mode": "edge-light",
    "drop_on_decrypt_failure": false,
    "tenant_policies": {
      "default": "buffered"
    }
  }
}
```
lucy: how will customers opt their tenants into strict? console + API? we should provide a sample SLA note and explain replay path for buffered events.
sasha: console + API toggle. replay path: customers can request replay of buffered raw events; requires decrypt role so we need RBAC + audit trail.
jordyn: cost numbers we saw in last run: decrypt CPU ~0.5 vCPU-second per 10k events, indexing IO cost ~$0.008 per 1k events for immediate indexing. batching and async indexing cut CPU by ~30% in our test.
amar: other optimization: canonicalize schema to shorten payloads (drop redundant keys) and encourage clients to batch at source. we can add client SDK helpers.
lucy: customer communication: clearly state that switching to buffered means events accepted but may be delayed for validation; strict will return 4xx on schema mismatch. include migration guide.
sasha: rollout plan: 1) canary edge prevalidation for 5 high-volume tenants (amar to prototype) 2) jordyn to add 503 backpressure + metrics and tenant burst tokens 3) lucy to draft API + console UX + customer comms 4) add RBAC role ingest:validate and ensure decrypt endpoints require it.
amar: will prototype edge verifier by EOD and push flag behind feature toggle.
jordyn: I'll wire in the 503 path and emit metrics: validation_failures, buffered_events_count, decrypt_time_ms distribution.
lucy: I'll start the customer-facing doc and sample messages.
sasha: solid. add follow-ups: decide retention for buffered raw drops and legal hold behavior. :thumbsup:
